statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42772 ("Potential CPU DoS via O(n^2) Fragment Reassembly in QUIC", Low) affects OpenSSL 3.5: QUIC stream reassembly slows down quadratically as stream frames arrive out of order, so a remote peer that completes the handshake can cause connection-scoped CPU pressure and possibly a denial of service with compliant STREAM frames and little bandwidth. OpenSSL fixed it in 3.5.9, and Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 (DSA-6531-1): https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260929.txt, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-42772. The advisory states that the FIPS modules are not affected because the QUIC implementation is outside the FIPS module boundary. The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI security repository (the FIPS builds and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build only in the security repository). The Debian changelog shipped in libssl3t64 was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64 (25 versions, packages verified against the index checksums). No build of Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-42772; the first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, the fixed boundary here, and every later build (the other rebuilds of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and of 3.5.9-1~deb13u1, and their FIPS builds) carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 entry naming it. The openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the same OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds.
